transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Start time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (CTO - Pinecrest), Sara Gomez (InfoSec Manager), Tom Ellis (SRE), Lena Wu (Compliance)

Summary: Weekly pilot security sync for Pinecrest Bank. Focus on SSO setup, audit logs, data retention windows during pilot, and SOC2 evidence access. Agreement on metadata exchange and follow-up deep-dive.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we are on for the weekly security sync, i'll just do a quick roll call — maya from redwood, liam from our se team.
[00:12] Raj Patel: hey thanks, raj here. sara, tom, lena on our side. thanks for keeping this on cadence.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: hey all, quick agenda - SSO status, audit log export and what fields we produce, retention settings for the pilot data, and then SOC2/control mapping questions. anything to add?
[00:28] Sara Gomez: no that covers it. main open items are the SAML metadata and forwarder for logs to our splunk instance. also need to validate that redwood's retention settings can be tuned per dataset.
[00:37] Maya Chen: great, so first SSO. liam walked through the SAML flow we recommended — it's standard SAML 2.0 with optional SCIM provision. i will send the metadata after the call. liam, do you want to add the nitty gritty?
[00:47] Liam O'Connor: yeah so in our dedicated pilot you can do either hosted with SAML or the private control-plane option. for pilot most customers use SAML + SCIM so you get user mapping and groups. note, our metadata endpoint has the entity id and cert, you'll upload that into your idp. we also support JIT provisioning if you don't want SCIM initially.
[00:58] Sara Gomez: question — can we map our internal AD groups to RBAC roles in redwood? we need least privilege for access to production-like datasets.
[01:07] Liam O'Connor: yes you can map SAML attributes or SCIM group names to RBAC roles. we have a role mapping table in the console; we'll send a screenshot. small caveat: if you use JIT you'll get a default role until SCIM is enabled.
[01:20] Tom Ellis: ok, and audit trails — what does the log look like? we need per-request context with user id, route, model id, tokens, and decision points for routing/fallbacks.
[01:32] Maya Chen: liam, show the audit example.
[01:34] Liam O'Connor: sure — (screen) our audit events include timestamp, request_id, user.subject/email, route/model, tokens_in/tokens_out approximate, latency_ms, decision_reason (like fallback-to-quantized-model), and sha256 of prompt if you enable hashing. we can forward logs to an S3 bucket for long-term retention or push via syslog/HTTP to splunk/sumo.
[01:53] Raj Patel: good. do you preserve the full prompt in logs by default? compliance wants redact-first option.
[01:58] Liam O'Connor: by default we store full request payload in the pilot's ephemeral store, but audit logs can be configured to either include full text, hashed text, or redacted placeholders. retention policy applies to both raw payload and processed audit logs.
[02:12] Sara Gomez: so for our pilot, we want hashed prompts in logs, keep raw for 7 days, audit events forwarded to splunk daily, and long-term retention 365 days for metadata only. can redwood support that?
[02:22] Liam O'Connor: yes — we support per-pipeline retention windows. we can set raw payload TTL to 7 days, retain audit metadata 365 days, and push daily batches to your splunk HTTP ingest. we'll send sample events so you can validate fields.
[02:36] Tom Ellis: on the splunk side we need a sample webhook and example events to map fields. i'll share the endpoint after the call.
[02:44] Maya Chen: perfect — that's on the action list. next, encryption and KMS. lena, any specific regs we need to meet?
[02:52] Lena Wu: we need AES-256 at rest for any customer data, KMS integration for key rotation logs, and ability to use our HSM for the private deployment. also we need to know whether redwood stores keys or if the customer manages keys.
[03:05] Liam O'Connor: for the dedicated/private options we support customer-managed keys via KMS. we have integrations with cloud KMS providers and can support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flows; for on-prem/HSM we run a connector that keeps keys in your HSM and redwood never sees plaintext. we'll share architecture doc.
[03:19] Raj Patel: excellent. SOC2 — we need evidence for specific controls around access, logging, and change management. do you have a mapping doc?
[03:27] Maya Chen: yes we have a SOC2 controls mapping spreadsheet we usually share. it maps redwood controls to typical customer controls. liam, note to attach that.
[03:34] Liam O'Connor: noted. also, if you want us to point to penetration test reports, we can share executive summaries under an NDA. full reports are generally on a need-to-know basis.
[03:44] Sara Gomez: we'll likely need the mapping and the SOC2 report excerpts. lisa? (sic) lena will coordinate internal review.
[03:50] Lena Wu: yep we'll review and list which evidences we need. if redwood can provide user activity logs for the pilot window that will help.
[03:57] Maya Chen: we can export user activity logs scoped to the pilot account. one note on export frequency — we support real-time streaming and daily batch exports. which do you prefer for compliance?
[04:08] Sara Gomez: daily batch is fine for now, real-time might be noisy for us. daily with redundancy is ideal.
[04:14] Liam O'Connor: ok we'll set up daily forwarding to splunk and provide a fallback S3 export for redundancy.
[04:20] Tom Ellis: about retention and deletion — we will want a documented process for deletion requests and proof of deletion if required by audit. can that be automated?
[04:29] Liam O'Connor: we support API-driven deletion for datasets and also we can provide deletion logs as part of audit export. deletion requests in the pilot are handled via the console or API and produce an audit event.
[04:40] Raj Patel: timeline — we need SAML tested by next week, hopefully SOC2 mapping the week after. are those realistic?
[04:47] Maya Chen: yes, realistic. we'll send metadata today and liam will enable a test IdP endpoint in the dedicated pilot. SOC2 mapping doc we can send by end of week and schedule the evidence deep-dive for next Tue.
[04:58] Sara Gomez: perfect. one more question — any rate limits or throttling in the pilot that we should know about? sometimes throttling can break retries in our platform.
[05:06] Liam O'Connor: pilot tiers have soft limits; for dedicated pilot we can provision higher quotas. we expose detailed headers for rate-limit information and retry-after in responses so your client can handle backoff. we'll share the quota table.
[05:18] Tom Ellis: thanks, that helps.
[05:20] Maya Chen: cool — let's recap next steps: maya send SAML metadata + idp guide; liam send sample audit events and splunk webhook example; sara share retention policy and tom give splunk endpoint; lena will list SOC2 evidence needs. schedule SOC2 evidence call for next tuesday.
[05:36] Raj Patel: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:38] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in the crm and slack. bye.
